=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible as paired leaves emerging from the same node on the stem in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely together at the terminal end of the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves consist of a single blade without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf edges are smooth and continuous, with no teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): obovate (leaf is broadest above the middle, tapering towards the base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaf tip comes to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base of the leaf is smoothly curved without a distinct angle or cleft)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with secondary veins branching off towards the margin)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): prominent, closely spaced, and numerous (forming a distinct reticulate pattern)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): rugose (surface is wrinkled and uneven due to the sunken secondary veins)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surface appears smooth and hairless)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is visibly shorter than the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole appears cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears hard, rigid, and brownish)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface is smooth)
    19. Stem color: brown
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf nodes)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint-like structure is visible at the petiole base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: Leaves exhibit numerous small brown spots and minor physical damage (holes and missing margins).
